title: A Ledger for the Inheritance
premise: Vesper Whitlock, concierge at the crumbling Meridian Hotel, is hired by a nervous guest named Ilse to prove that Ilse's sister Marta—who everyone in the coastal town insists drowned a decade ago—is still alive. Vesper discovers the 'drowning' was staged by the family to seize an inheritance, and that Marta has been hiding in plain sight as the hotel's night porter, her memory shattered. As the tide recedes to expose a sunken car and the truth inside it, Vesper must protect Marta from the cousin who needs her declared dead, ending with Marta reclaiming her name and Vesper gaining the family they never believed they'd have.
about_author: Noor Sandoval is a former night-shift hotel clerk who spent years collecting the secrets guests leave behind at front desks. They write mysteries about the people the world overlooks, from a small apartment above a laundromat.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A guest named Ilse arrives at the Meridian with an envelope of cash and an impossible request: prove her sister Marta, drowned ten years ago, is still alive. Vesper, who has quietly solved three 'accidents,' takes the case against their better judgment. Emotional beat: wary curiosity hardening into commitment as Vesper notices Ilse flinches at her own family's name.

chapters.title: What the Register Remembers
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Digging through old ledgers, Vesper finds Marta checked into the Meridian the very night she 'drowned'—and realizes the night porter, silent Ruth, signs her timesheets in Marta's handwriting. The cousin Aldous arrives hunting the inheritance paperwork. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery curdling into fear as Vesper understands Ruth/Marta remembers nothing and someone wants it kept that way.

chapters.title: Before the Tide Turns
chapters.summary: Ruth/Marta's POV, fragmented and dreamlike, interwoven with Vesper's. Aldous confronts Vesper; Ilse disappears, and Vesper fears she betrayed them—until her abandoned notes reveal she was lured out. The spring tide begins to recede, exposing the roof of a sunken car offshore. Emotional beat: dread and tenderness as Marta's memory flickers alive and Vesper vows to stand between her and the past.

chapters.title: A Ledger for the Inheritance
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The tide gives up the car and the confession hidden inside it—Aldous's father drowned there, and the family buried the crime by erasing Marta. Confronted in the hotel lobby with witnesses, ledgers, and Ilse returned, Aldous breaks. Marta signs her own name for the first time in ten years. Emotional beat: grief giving way to belonging, as Vesper realizes the Meridian's misfits have become a family.
